# Terraform Provider OpenAI [![Latest Release](https://img.shields.io/github/release/cloudopsworks/terraform-provider-openai.svg?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/cloudopsworks/terraform-provider-openai/releases/latest) [![Terraform Registry](https://img.shields.io/badge/registry-cloudopsworks%2Fopenai-844FBA?style=for-the-badge&logo=terraform)](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/cloudopsworks/openai/latest) [![OpenTofu](https://img.shields.io/badge/OpenTofu-compatible-FFDA18?style=for-the-badge&logo=opentofu&logoColor=black)](https://opentofu.org) [![Go Report Card](https://goreportcard.com/badge/github.com/cloudopsworks/terraform-provider-openai?style=for-the-badge)](https://goreportcard.com/report/github.com/cloudopsworks/terraform-provider-openai) [![Last Updated](https://img.shields.io/github/last-commit/cloudopsworks/terraform-provider-openai.svg?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/cloudopsworks/terraform-provider-openai/commits)


Terraform/OpenTofu provider for OpenAI Administration APIs. It manages projects,
project service accounts, service-account project API keys, organization admin
API keys, groups, group membership, organization/project custom roles, and
user/group role assignments using an existing OpenAI admin API key supplied
directly, from OpenAI environment variables, or resolved from AWS Secrets
Manager, Google Secret Manager, or Azure Key Vault.


---

## Introduction

This provider turns OpenAI organization administration into reviewed
infrastructure-as-code: create projects, create service accounts, issue project
API keys, rotate admin API keys, organize users into groups, and manage
organization/project roles and role assignments.

Organization users are exposed as data sources because the current OpenAI Go SDK
does not expose a user creation endpoint. User access is managed through group
membership and role assignment resources, while the provider continues to
consume an existing bootstrap admin key from configuration, environment
variables, or a cloud secret manager without storing that resolved provider key
in Terraform state.

## Usage



## Provider configuration

The provider resolves OpenAI initialization settings in this precedence order:

1. Explicit provider arguments: `admin_api_key`, `base_url`, `organization_id`, and `project_id`.
2. OpenAI environment variables: `OPENAI_ADMIN_KEY`, `OPENAI_BASE_URL`, `OPENAI_ORG_ID`, and `OPENAI_PROJECT_ID`.
3. One cloud secret source when no direct/admin environment key is present.

Secret payloads may be either plaintext (the admin API key) or a JSON object.
JSON payloads can include `admin_api_key` or `api_key`, plus optional
`base_url`, `organization_id`, and `project_id`; explicit provider arguments
and OpenAI environment variables still win for fields they set.

Direct configuration:

```hcl
provider "openai" {
  admin_api_key   = var.openai_admin_api_key
  organization_id = var.openai_org_id
  project_id      = var.openai_project_id
}
```

AWS Secrets Manager with an assumed role:

```hcl
provider "openai" {
  aws_secrets_manager = {
    region            = "us-east-1"
    secret_id         = "prod/openai/admin"
    role_arn          = "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/openai-secret-reader"
    role_session_name = "terraform-provider-openai"
    external_id       = var.aws_external_id
    json_key          = "admin_api_key"
  }
}
```

The AWS source uses the standard AWS SDK credential chain as the base
credential and supports environment discovery with variables such as
`OPENAI_AWS_SECRETS_MANAGER_SECRET_ID`, `OPENAI_AWS_SECRETS_MANAGER_REGION`,
`OPENAI_AWS_SECRETS_MANAGER_ROLE_ARN`, and
`OPENAI_AWS_SECRETS_MANAGER_JSON_KEY`. Raw AWS access keys are not provider
arguments.

GCP Secret Manager with service-account impersonation:

```hcl
provider "openai" {
  gcp_secret_manager = {
    project_id                  = "platform-prod"
    secret_id                   = "openai-admin-key"
    version                     = "latest"
    impersonate_service_account = "openai-secret-reader@platform-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com"
    json_key                    = "admin_api_key"
  }
}
```

The GCP source uses Application Default Credentials as the base credential and
can impersonate a service account. Environment discovery uses variables such
as `OPENAI_GCP_SECRET_MANAGER_PROJECT_ID`,
`OPENAI_GCP_SECRET_MANAGER_SECRET_ID`,
`OPENAI_GCP_SECRET_MANAGER_IMPERSONATE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT`, and
`OPENAI_GCP_SECRET_MANAGER_JSON_KEY`. Raw service-account JSON is not a
provider argument.

Azure Key Vault:

```hcl
provider "openai" {
  azure_key_vault = {
    vault_url   = "https://platform-prod.vault.azure.net/"
    secret_name = "openai-admin-key"
    json_key    = "admin_api_key"
  }
}
```

When no direct admin key is configured, configure only one cloud secret source.
If AWS and GCP secret discovery are both complete, provider configuration fails
with a deterministic conflict diagnostic. Malformed JSON payloads and missing
selected `json_key` fields are hard diagnostics; optional JSON fields simply
fall back to explicit provider arguments, environment variables, or defaults.

## Bootstrap one internal application

```hcl
resource "openai_project" "app" {
  name = "search-prod"
}

resource "openai_service_account" "app" {
  project_id = openai_project.app.id
  name       = "search-prod"
  role       = "member"
}

resource "openai_project_api_key" "app" {
  project_id         = openai_project.app.id
  service_account_id = openai_service_account.app.id
  name               = "search-prod"
}
```

`openai_project_api_key.value` is Sensitive and returned only at create time.
Protect Terraform state accordingly.

## Organization access management

```hcl
resource "openai_admin_api_key" "automation" {
  name = "terraform-automation"

  lifecycle {
    prevent_destroy = true
  }
}

data "openai_organization_user" "alice" {
  id = "user_123"
}

resource "openai_organization_group" "engineering" {
  name = "Engineering"
}

resource "openai_organization_group_user" "engineering_alice" {
  group_id = openai_organization_group.engineering.id
  user_id  = data.openai_organization_user.alice.id
}

resource "openai_organization_role" "auditor" {
  name        = "auditor"
  description = "Read-only organization auditor"
  permissions = ["organization.users.read"]
}

resource "openai_organization_group_role" "engineering_auditor" {
  group_id = openai_organization_group.engineering.id
  role_id  = openai_organization_role.auditor.id
}
```

Admin API keys and critical access roles should use Terraform lifecycle
protection such as `prevent_destroy` when accidental removal would lock out
automation or operators.
